newsitem.title: FRANCE: British girl's parents seek fresh murder probe.
newsitem.headline: British girl's parents seek fresh murder probe.

text.p: The parents of British teenager Caroline Dickinson, who was raped and strangled in a youth hostel in western France almost a year ago, have filed a fresh lawsuit to demand further investigations into her unsolved murder, justice sources said on Saturday.

Dickinson, aged 13, of Launceston, Cornwall, was on a school trip to Britanny when she was attacked by an unidentified man while other girls slept in her dormitory in Pleine-Fougeres, near the historic Mont Saint-Michel, last July 18.
Police arrested a homeless local man a few days later but released him after he retracted a confession made under interrogation and DNA tests cleared him.

The sources said Herve Rouzaud-Legoff, a lawyer acting for the girl's family, filed a formal application on Friday for wider genetic testing, a public appeal for witnesses and the linking of the investigation with another probe into a sex attack a youth hostel a few kilometres away on the same night.
A few hours earlier, a man broke into a hostel in Saint-Lunaire, where another British school group was staying, but fled without being identified after being disturbed by some of the schoolchildren.
The Dickinsons' lawyer called for more systematic genetic testing to be conducted in the Pleine-Fougeres area in line with British practice in such cases.

French gendarmes have conducted about 250 ADN tests in the last year on the staff and residents of the youth hostel, the schoolchidren in Caroline's group and other suspects detained in cases of sex offences and exhibitionism.
The Dickinson family is also seeking to have investigating magistrate Gerard Zaug and the gendarmerie taken off the case, arguing that they had made several mistakes in the probe.
The parents are due to meet junior British Foreign Office minister Baroness Symonds on Tuesday to seek government help in pressing their case.
